atoms.b: In the decimal system, the position of the digits of a number plays an important role. The number 531 consists of 1 3 ++5 hundreds, 1 ++3 5 tens and a one.
Each digit is 10 times larger than the digit to its right. The first digit is multiplied once, the second ten times, the third ((ten ++one_hundred one_thousand)) times and so on.
The binary system works in a similar way. However, the value of the digit is multiplied once, twice, ((three ++four five)) times and so on with each place you move along.

instruction.text: In the binary system, each digit has twice the value of the previous digit. Fill in the table accordingly.
Convert the number <mat>(`1000`)_2</mat> into a decimal number.
instruction.sound: Convert the binary number one zero zero zero into a decimal number.

hint.text: The zeros in a binary number can be skipped during conversion. Whenever a 0 occurs in a binary number, the corresponding place is multiplied by 0.

atoms.a: In which place is the <mat>1</mat> in <mat>(`1000`)_2</mat>?

Is there another <mat>1</mat> in the binary number <mat>(`1000`)_2</mat>?
Which decimal number does <mat>(`1000`)_2</mat> correspond to?

instruction.text: Match the binary numbers to the corresponding decimal numbers.

trainers.instruction: Which two numbers are the only ones that have the same representation in the decimal and binary systems?
trainers.hint: Consider which digits are used in the binary system. The numbers you are looking for must only consist of these digits.
